newsitem.title: UK: Brady market lacks direction in limited trade.
newsitem.headline: Brady market lacks direction in limited trade.

text.p: The Brady market failed to inspire dealers on Thursday with little fresh news to push prices, they said.
"It is very quiet, there's nothing special to mention," a dealer said.
An analyst at a U.S. bank said emerging markets looked a touch vulnerable.
"Spreads widened quite extensively on Wednesday through London and New York trade which has left emerging markets looking good but just a touch vulnerable."
He said the U.S. had a slew of data due next week: "So everyone will be cautious and wondering how much more short-term upside there is."
Dealers said news that Vietnam plans to issue bonds at the end of June as part of a deal to restructure its multi-million-dollar debt to foreign banks had little impact on the market.

"There is mixed news on Vietnam because there are also reports on Vietnam's bad debt management," a South East Asia specialist said, adding there were more Bradies in the pipeline from Vietnam, the Ivory Coast and Bolivia.
Analysts said the deal, a signal of Vietnam's willingness to repay its debts, would put the spotlight onto the country's long-held ambition to tap the Eurobond market for funds.
Sources said they expected Vietnam's first Eurobond would probably total between $100 million and $150 million, with a maturity of either three or five years.
